title: Intergenerational Support in Modern Families
fullTitle: IELTS Hourly Practice — Topic 15: Family, relationships, and social issues — Intergenerational Support in Modern Families

sections.title: Vocabulary: family support and social issues
sections.html:
Use these terms to discuss modern family duties, social pressure, and public support. Section A is Band 6.5–7.5; Section B is Band 7.5–9.0.

Hãy dùng các thuật ngữ này để bàn về trách nhiệm gia đình hiện đại, áp lực xã hội và hỗ trợ công. Phần A ở Band 6.5–7.5; Phần B ở Band 7.5–9.0.

items.definition: practical or emotional help between different age groups in a family
items.translation: sự hỗ trợ giữa các thế hệ
items.example: Intergenerational support can reduce pressure on both young parents and older relatives.
items.example_vi: Sự hỗ trợ giữa các thế hệ có thể giảm áp lực cho cả cha mẹ trẻ và người thân lớn tuổi.

items.definition: the physical, emotional, or financial pressure of looking after someone
items.example: The caregiving burden often falls on family members who already work full-time.
items.example_vi: Gánh nặng chăm sóc thường rơi vào các thành viên gia đình đã làm việc toàn thời gian.

items.definition: the ability to recover from stress or difficult feelings
items.translation: khả năng phục hồi cảm xúc
items.example: Strong family ties can build emotional resilience during periods of uncertainty.
items.example_vi: Quan hệ gia đình bền chặt có thể xây dựng khả năng phục hồi cảm xúc trong giai đoạn bất ổn.

items.definition: limits that separate job responsibilities from personal life
items.translation: ranh giới giữa công việc và cuộc sống
items.example: Remote work makes work-life boundaries harder to maintain.
items.example_vi: Làm việc từ xa khiến ranh giới giữa công việc và cuộc sống khó duy trì hơn.

items.definition: a duty divided fairly among several people
items.example: Childcare should be treated as a shared responsibility, not a private struggle.
items.example_vi: Chăm sóc trẻ em nên được xem là trách nhiệm chung, không phải cuộc vật lộn riêng tư.

items.definition: a lack of regular contact or meaningful relationships with other people
items.example: Social isolation can affect older adults even when they live in crowded cities.
items.example_vi: Sự cô lập xã hội có thể ảnh hưởng đến người cao tuổi ngay cả khi họ sống ở thành phố đông đúc.

items.definition: care that goes both ways between people, rather than only one direction
items.example: Healthy families often depend on reciprocal care across generations.
items.example_vi: Các gia đình lành mạnh thường dựa vào sự chăm sóc qua lại giữa các thế hệ.

items.definition: a situation in which someone relies on another person for money
items.example: Long-term financial dependency can create tension between adults and their parents.
items.example_vi: Sự phụ thuộc tài chính dài hạn có thể tạo căng thẳng giữa người trưởng thành và cha mẹ.

items.definition: local support that helps people when family or income is insufficient
items.translation: mạng lưới an sinh cộng đồng
items.example: A community safety net can protect families facing sudden illness or unemployment.
items.example_vi: Mạng lưới an sinh cộng đồng có thể bảo vệ các gia đình đối mặt với bệnh tật hoặc thất nghiệp đột ngột.

items.definition: discussion within a family about roles, money, time, and decisions
items.translation: sự thương lượng trong gia đình
items.example: Household negotiation is essential when several generations live together.
items.example_vi: Sự thương lượng trong gia đình là thiết yếu khi nhiều thế hệ sống cùng nhau.

sections.title: Reading: Shared care in modern families
sections.html:
Modern families are often described as smaller and more independent than those in the past, but this does not mean that family support has disappeared. In many societies, it has simply become more complicated. Young adults may live far from their parents for education or work, while older relatives may need help with transport, technology, or health appointments. At the same time, parents of young children may depend on grandparents for childcare because formal services are expensive or unavailable. This pattern can create real benefits. Intergenerational support allows knowledge, money, time, and emotional reassurance to move in more than one direction. Grandparents may provide stability for children, while younger relatives may help older adults avoid social isolation. In strong families, reciprocal care can make people feel useful rather than dependent. However, the system is fragile when support is expected but not discussed. One adult child may carry most of the caregiving burden because siblings live elsewhere. A grandparent may enjoy helping with childcare but feel unable to refuse extra hours. Couples may argue when work-life boundaries disappear and every family need becomes urgent. Without household negotiation, love can turn into resentment. Public policy also matters. Governments should not assume that families can solve every social problem privately. Affordable childcare, flexible work, eldercare services, and community centres can reduce pressure while still respecting family bonds. The goal is not to replace the family, but to prevent support from becoming sacrifice. A modern family works best when care is shared, visible, and realistic.

Gia đình hiện đại thường được mô tả là nhỏ hơn và độc lập hơn so với quá khứ, nhưng điều này không có nghĩa là sự hỗ trợ gia đình đã biến mất. Ở nhiều xã hội, nó chỉ trở nên phức tạp hơn. Người trẻ có thể sống xa cha mẹ để học tập hoặc làm việc, trong khi người thân lớn tuổi có thể cần giúp đỡ về đi lại, công nghệ hoặc lịch khám sức khỏe.

questions.q: 1. Why has family support become more complicated?
questions.answer: Because people often live far apart while different generations still need practical support.
questions.explanation: The passage mentions young adults living far away and older relatives needing help.

questions.q: 2. Grandparents may help children while younger relatives may reduce older adults’ isolation. True, False, or Not Given?
questions.explanation: Both examples are directly stated in paragraph two.

questions.q: 3. What can happen when support is expected but not discussed? A lower taxes B resentment C more formal services D fewer appointments
questions.explanation: The passage says love can turn into resentment without negotiation.

questions.q: 4. Name one public policy that can reduce family pressure.
questions.answer: Affordable childcare, flexible work, eldercare services, or community centres.
questions.explanation: Any one of these is named in the final paragraph.

questions.q: 5. The writer believes governments should replace family bonds. True, False, or Not Given?
questions.explanation: The writer says the goal is not to replace the family.

sections.title: Listening: Community family support programme
sections.html:
Today we’re looking at the new family support programme at the community centre. I want to emphasize one point first: this is not only for elderly residents, although some early posters gave that impression. The programme is designed for households where different generations depend on one another in practical ways. On Monday evenings, there will be a technology help desk. Teenagers from the local college will help older residents use online banking, hospital portals, and video calls. Please note that the sessions begin at six fifteen, not six o’clock as printed in the first newsletter. On Wednesday mornings, parents of young children can attend a short advice session about childcare options and work-life boundaries. Children can come too, but the centre cannot provide full babysitting during that session. The most popular activity may be the Saturday family workshop. It was originally planned as a cooking class, but after feedback it has been changed to household budgeting and communication. Families will discuss how to divide costs, time, and caregiving tasks more fairly. Attendance is free for residents of the district. People from outside the district can join only if spaces remain after registration closes on Friday. Volunteers will also collect suggestions for future sessions at the reception desk.

Hôm nay chúng ta xem xét chương trình hỗ trợ gia đình mới tại trung tâm cộng đồng. Trước tiên tôi muốn nhấn mạnh một điểm: chương trình này không chỉ dành cho cư dân cao tuổi, mặc dù một số áp phích ban đầu đã tạo ấn tượng như vậy. Chương trình được thiết kế cho các hộ gia đình mà các thế hệ khác nhau phụ thuộc vào nhau theo những cách thực tế.

questions.q: 1. Who is the programme designed for?
questions.answer: Households where different generations depend on one another.
questions.explanation: Trap: it is not only for elderly residents.

questions.q: 2. What time does the Monday technology help desk begin?
3. What topic is covered on Wednesday morning?
questions.explanation: This is stated in the Wednesday session description.

questions.q: 4. What was the Saturday workshop originally planned as?

questions.explanation: Outside-district residents can join only if spaces remain after registration closes on Friday.

sections.title: Writing Task 2
sections.prompt: Some people argue that adult children should be mainly responsible for caring for elderly parents, while others believe the state should provide most eldercare. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
sections.html:
Care for elderly people should involve both families and the state, because each can provide a type of support that the other cannot fully replace. In my view, adult children have moral responsibilities, but governments must create reliable services so that care does not become an unfair private burden. On the one hand, family care is emotionally powerful. Elderly parents may feel safer and more respected when they receive help from people who understand their habits, values, and medical history. Adult children can notice small changes in mood or health more quickly than a distant institution. In many cultures, supporting parents is also seen as a way to repay years of sacrifice. This sense of reciprocal care can strengthen family identity across generations. On the other hand, relying mainly on adult children is not always realistic. Many people live far from their parents, work long hours, or have young children of their own. If one sibling becomes the main caregiver, the caregiving burden may damage their career, finances, and emotional resilience. In addition, some elderly people need professional medical or psychological support that relatives are not trained to provide. Therefore, the best solution is shared responsibility. Families should offer regular contact, emotional support, and help with decisions, while the state should fund affordable home care, day centres, transport, and emergency services. Employers can also contribute through flexible working arrangements. Overall, eldercare should not be treated as either a family duty or a government duty alone. A humane society allows families to remain close without forcing them to carry responsibilities beyond their capacity.

Việc chăm sóc người cao tuổi nên có cả gia đình và nhà nước tham gia, vì mỗi bên có thể cung cấp một kiểu hỗ trợ mà bên kia không thể thay thế hoàn toàn. Theo tôi, con cái trưởng thành có trách nhiệm đạo đức, nhưng chính phủ phải tạo ra dịch vụ đáng tin cậy để việc chăm sóc không trở thành gánh nặng riêng tư bất công.
structure: Body 1: emotional value of family care
Body 2: practical limits of relying on adult children
Body 3: combined solution with services and flexibility
Conclusion: family closeness without excessive burden
improvement_notes: Avoid an extreme position; IELTS rewards a realistic balance here.
Use precise terms such as reciprocal care, caregiving burden, and shared responsibility.
Give practical policy examples instead of only emotional arguments.

part1.q: Do you spend much time with your family?
part1.sample:
I try to, although work can make it difficult. Even short conversations help me feel connected and emotionally grounded.

Tôi cố gắng, mặc dù công việc có thể khiến điều đó khó khăn. Ngay cả những cuộc trò chuyện ngắn cũng giúp tôi cảm thấy gắn kết và ổn định về cảm xúc.

part1.q: How do families support each other in your country?
part1.sample:
Many families share childcare, financial advice, and help with important decisions, especially when several generations live close together.

Nhiều gia đình chia sẻ việc chăm sóc trẻ, lời khuyên tài chính và hỗ trợ quyết định quan trọng, đặc biệt khi nhiều thế hệ sống gần nhau.

part2.cue_card: Describe an older person in your family who has influenced you.
part2.prep: Say who the person is, what they did for the family, how you supported them, and why you admire them.
part2.long_turn:
I’d like to talk about my grandmother, because she played a very important role in my family when I was growing up. She was not only an elderly relative who needed respect; she was also someone who gave practical and emotional support to everyone around her. When my parents were busy with work, she often helped prepare meals and looked after the children after school. What I remember most is not a dramatic event, but the daily sense of stability she created. She had a calm way of speaking, and whenever there was a small conflict in the family, she could make people slow down and think more carefully. At the same time, the support was not one-way. As she became older, younger family members helped her with transport, hospital visits, and using a smartphone to contact relatives. This made me realize that healthy families depend on reciprocal care. Different generations may have different strengths, but everyone can contribute something. I admire her because she showed that family responsibility does not have to feel cold or forced. It can be expressed through ordinary actions, such as cooking, listening, giving advice, or simply being present. In my opinion, those small acts are what make family relationships meaningful over time.

Tôi muốn nói về bà của tôi, vì bà đóng vai trò rất quan trọng trong gia đình khi tôi lớn lên. Bà không chỉ là một người thân cao tuổi cần được tôn trọng; bà còn là người mang lại sự hỗ trợ thực tế và tinh thần cho mọi người xung quanh.

part3.q: Are young people today less responsible for their parents than in the past?
part3.sample:
Not necessarily. They may express responsibility differently because work, migration, and housing costs have changed family life.

Không hẳn. Họ có thể thể hiện trách nhiệm theo cách khác vì công việc, di cư và chi phí nhà ở đã thay đổi đời sống gia đình.

part3.q: Should governments support unpaid family caregivers?
part3.sample:
Yes. Training, respite care, and financial allowances can prevent caregivers from becoming exhausted or economically vulnerable.

Có. Đào tạo, chăm sóc thay thế tạm thời và trợ cấp tài chính có thể ngăn người chăm sóc kiệt sức hoặc dễ tổn thương về kinh tế.

sections.title: Topic strategy note
sections.html:
For Topic 15, avoid only saying that family is important. Develop both emotional and practical dimensions: distance, time, money, childcare, eldercare, and social isolation.

Với Chủ đề 15, tránh chỉ nói gia đình quan trọng. Hãy phát triển cả khía cạnh cảm xúc và thực tế: khoảng cách, thời gian, tiền bạc, chăm sóc trẻ, chăm sóc người già và cô lập xã hội.
